behaviors.description: The iOS title screen retains the automatic material showcases: dirt, established rooted turf, fine sand, pebbles, a generated trunk split along grain, the same trunk chopped across grain, stone, loose stone, and broad bucket contact against stone, plus a coupled turf/soil/bedrock excavation sequence. Finite-force spade, bucket, axe and pick trajectories act through their material solvers. Turf reports severed roots, pieces and lifted tissue; wood reports directional failures and contact work. Native controls observe, pause, single-step, reset or exit. Sparse seedling growth and the earlier soil fixtures remain separately selectable on desktop. The workshop shows measured wall-clock FPS, simulation speed relative to real time, CPU physics, mesh and render/present cost. Fixed 1/60-second physical frames are scheduled by wall time with bounded catch-up. Pause and unchanged frames do not rebuild meshes. The mobile Compare forces selector runs three fresh specimens at different actuator limits; the desktop catalog exposes corresponding _compare cases. Trial captions retain measured results and distinguish commanded force from actual contact. The iOS bridge validates choices against the engine case registry. Five additional entries expose a third-person worker digging, a worker chopping a standing tree, worker snow shoveling, ice in warm water and ice in air. Worker captions show measured contact and effort; thermal captions label accelerated heat time. Force-comparison variants remain limited to the previous supported specimens. Combined workshop appearance has a bounded 32768-triangle envelope for worker, tool and material; this does not increase physics mesh budgets.
behaviors.selection: Material workshop choices on the iOS title screen, or matter_* desktop workshop cases. The mobile and Mac workshop selectors provide WebGPU (default), Vulkan and OpenGL explicitly; there is no silent backend fallback.

checks.expectation: The selected automatic material scene is visible and distinguishable, with functioning camera, pause, step, reset, background/resume and exit. Soil extraction leaves a cavity and released matter persists. Stage captions report requested motion separately from measured state. Failures retain the last valid state.
checks.procedure: Compile the iOS target. The user performs runtime and visual playtesting: observe insertion, fracture, lift, release, reset, background/resume and exit. The new fracture showcase remains behaviorally unverified until that playtest; the prior contact-only phone observation does not verify it.

checks.expectation: All three explicitly selected backends render material scenes. The counter distinguishes render throughput from simulation throughput; bounded desktop and headless runs write timing summaries including frame percentiles and material/contact/skin costs. Fixed physical substeps and iteration counts are retained.
checks.procedure: Run release-mode before/after headless benchmarks and bounded WebGPU/Vulkan/OpenGL workshop runs on macOS. Compile iOS and UIKit. Phone timing remains a user playtest.

behaviors.description: Measure the same material advancement used by the visual workshop, excluding window and rendering costs. Report the requested and completed simulation work, CPU timing and real-time factor; errors or halted physics remain failures.

checks.expectation: The output contains finite wall and simulated time, step percentiles and halt state. Headless steps per second are not claimed as display FPS.
checks.procedure: Run bounded release-mode material cases and inspect the written JSON summaries.
